version.changelog:
hit-preview v1.0.2

- 升级为零配置即下载即用版本，无需 npm install 或 build。
- 预编译并打包完整依赖，支持一键运行与运行脚本。
- 智能降级本地算法，AI不可用时自动兜底分析。
- 增强 parseAIResponse 兼容性与 callAPI 错误处理。
- 文档聚焦核心爆款分析与常见短剧平台适配。

llm.summary: This skill mostly does the advertised AI script analysis, but it needs review because it handles model credentials, sends scripts to external AI APIs, prints part of an API key, and adds an undisclosed promotional link to results.

dimensions.detail: Reading ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json is disclosed and purpose-aligned, but the implementation also uses environment/profile API keys and prints a key prefix during diagnostics, which is unnecessary exposure.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The SKILL metadata references an install script named setup-zero-config.sh that is not present, while package.json points to missing dist files; the included wrapper instead runs bundle.js, so installation/runtime metadata is incoherent.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Commands are user-directed and input length is bounded, but the skill does not clearly ask before sending script content to configured external model providers or before using local OpenClaw/profile credentials.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: I found no evidence of persistence, background workers, privilege escalation, destructive file changes, or broad local indexing; local file access is limited to explicit script inputs and OpenClaw configuration.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The core script-analysis, scoring, comparison, and danmaku-generation behavior matches the stated purpose, but normal output paths append an unrelated promotional link that is not disclosed in SKILL.md.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Only use it with scripts you are comfortable sending to your configured AI provider, avoid running diagnostics in shared logs until the API-key-prefix output is fixed, and treat the embedded promotional link as unaudited external content.
llm.findings:
[TP4] unexpected: The scanner correctly identified a combination of config/credential use, external model calls, and promotional output; the model calls are purpose-aligned, but the undisclosed promotional footer is not.
[SSD-3] unexpected: Confirmed that diagnostic output prints the first ten characters of the configured API key, which is not needed for connection testing.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The same API-key-prefix logging concern is supported by bundle.js; I did not find evidence that the full key is printed.
[SQP-2] expected: Automatic OpenClaw config reading is disclosed in SKILL.md and fits the zero-config model-selection purpose, but there is no clear consent gate or no-read mode.
[E1] expected: Sending user script text to the configured AI provider is expected for AI analysis, but users should understand unpublished scripts may leave the machine.
[LP3] expected: Network and local credential access are coherent with the advertised OpenClaw integration, but the artifacts do not define tight permission boundaries or destination controls.
[T01] unexpected: Confirmed the static finding that default analysis and danmaku results include an undisclosed third-party promotional URL.
[T09] unexpected: Confirmed the static finding that the test command exposes an API key prefix in terminal output.
[SC1] unexpected: package.json uses caret dependency ranges; this is dependency hygiene risk, not evidence of malicious behavior.
[SC4] unexpected: Unpinned dependencies make exact resolved versions unverifiable from package.json alone, but this did not drive the verdict by itself.
